decisions.executionNote: Memorize red-left and blue-right poses; begin elbow-up approach arcs with open grippers, preserving separate workspaces.

Bring both grippers closer above their stems while continuing downward alignment, with clearance before descent.
Finish vertical approach orientations above each block and center over the remembered locations before lowering.
Use wrist views to correct lateral centering and stem angle while descending partway; final grasp height will be checked visually.
Lower slowly to stem grasp height; small wrist-image centering and angular corrections before closing.
Center the narrow stems between the fingers and close both grippers at table grasp height; retention remains to be tested by lifting.
Hold both grippers closed, then make a short vertical test lift to check that both blocks follow in RGB.

Replan smaller from the accepted prefix: move red toward far midline staging while blue waits back and right, with both retained closed.
Set red gently onto the far midline staging point; keep blue suspended clear on the right.
Release red at the midline staging site and begin a straight lift; blue remains held without crossing the arms.
Clear the left hand from staged red. Move held blue toward a second, nearer midline staging location, rotating toward red's remembered angle.
Withdraw the free left hand for clearance while carrying blue closer to the near midline and continuing its target-orientation turn.
Bring blue above the near midline staging point with its stem aligned to red's original direction; keep left clear.
Set blue gently at the near midline staging site, maintaining its red-target orientation and holding until table contact.
Release blue on the near staging site, then lift the empty right gripper before changing which arm handles each block.
Move the empty right hand outward and upward clear of blue; shift the left approach toward blue's near staging row without crossing.
Approach the two staged blocks from opposite sides: left toward near blue, right toward far red, separated in depth.
Center over blue and red staging sites from the left and right respectively, with vertical clearance and no arm crossing.
After the continuity stop, use smaller increments to center each gripper above its staged block and descend cautiously.
Use wrist views to align both staged stems and lower to grasp height, keeping the hands on opposite sides of the midline.
Close the left gripper on blue and the right on red at the staging sites, with small final lateral centering; next verify retention by lifting.
Keep both grippers fully commanded closed and test-lift the exchanged blocks vertically before transporting to the remembered targets.
Both blocks remain fixed in the wrist views during the test lift. Carry blue left and red right toward the remembered positions, turning red toward blue's original orientation.
Translate the exchanged blocks above their opposite original locations while finishing most of red's orientation change; keep both grips closed.
Lower blue toward red's remembered pose first, keeping red higher for wrist clearance; refine red's yaw and lateral position from the head view.
Set blue down and release it at the left target. Lower red to the right target with small perspective-based position corrections, retaining red until contact.
Finish gentle red placement and open its gripper. Lift the empty left hand to inspect blue's settled pose without disturbing either block.
Withdraw both open hands upward and outward, revealing the placed blocks for comparison with their memorized target silhouettes.
The settled silhouettes closely match the opposite starting poses. Begin smooth elbow-up return arcs with both hands open and clear of the blocks.
Continue the open-handed return, drawing both arms outward and back while smoothly restoring their home orientations.
Continue controlled return toward the memorized home poses, with both open grippers well clear of the swapped blocks.
Ease both arms back and downward along continuous return paths; maintain open hands and preserve the placed block poses.
Approach both home poses with reduced translation increments, keeping elbow configuration continuous and grippers open.
